reference_action: Borderline otherwise-healthy plant with one damaged lower leaf; owner reports larger growth and carefully removing the worsening leaf. Count local damaged-leaf removal, not an unconfirmed watering/light change.

sources.reason: Move away from direct light and halve watering; no instruction to trim the damaged leaf. The poster’s own removal history is not advice and did not solve their case.
Gently remove yellowing basal leaves; a few old leaves are normal.
5:09–6:11 explicitly recognizes normal old-leaf shedding and snips browning leaves with clean shears.
Remove brown-spotted affected leaves with clean scissors; same local removal action though with unnecessary disease alternatives.
Moisture/nutrient/heat/mineral-residue remedies but no leaf removal instruction.

resolved.reason: Sun stress is plausible but advice treats a generally healthy plant as needing multiple routine changes and omits confirmed trimming. The winter adjustment is poorly matched to stated hot months.

harmfulness.reason: “Take your watering down to half” is not supported by a soil check and is framed for winter despite the hot-month question. Moving ten feet from windows could reduce light excessively, though no destructive treatment is prescribed.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The source concerns escalating damage across more than twenty Pilea leaves. Its sunlight hypothesis overlaps the reference, but it misses the mild isolated-leaf case and otherwise-healthy status.

feasibility.reason: Moving the pot is straightforward. Halving an unspecified watering amount and an incomplete “only water when” comment leave the owner without a reliable moisture rule.
